findings.title: Duplicated "want has no end date" check
findings.description: `coverage_reads()` in `scripts/cutover_304_evidence.py` loops over `TICK_UNIVERSE`, raises `CutoverError` for an open-ended want, and builds the `{product} {schema} want has no end date` message. `latest_want_end()` in `scripts/purchase_verdicts.py:56-68` repeats the same loop, check and message. The project rules require DRY. One shared helper that yields `(entry, want)` pairs with an end date would give a single place to change. It would also remove the need for two separate tests of the same rule.

findings.title: New tests use bare generics, which strict pyright rejects
findings.description:
The Python rules require strict pyright over tests, with zero errors as a merge blocker. `test_purchase_verdicts.py` has several loose annotations:
- `_request(...) -> dict`
- `_unit(...) -> dict`
- `_coverage(...) -> dict`
- `exhausted: list | None`
- `units: list[dict] | None`
- `_status(...) -> object`

These are `reportMissingTypeArgument` errors under strict mode. Use `dict[str, Any]` and `list[ExhaustedRequest]`, or `Sequence[Any]`.

findings.title: `cutover_304_evidence.py` is over the ~300-line guideline
findings.description: The file is now 312 lines. `collect()` (about 40 lines) and `_family_evidence()` (about 35 lines) are near or over the ~50-line and 20-line targets. The `purchase_verdicts` and `purchase_accounting` split was meant to avoid this. Moving `coverage_reads` and `_family_evidence` into one of those modules would bring the file back under the limit.

findings.title: Script names no longer match their scope
findings.description: The docstring now says the script is shared by every purchase slice, and it takes `--slice`. The module, its tests and the `cutover_304_*` imports still carry the `304` name. This is not wrong. It will mislead readers as more purchase slices reuse it, so a rename is worth considering once 307 is closed.

findings.title: `SystemExit` caught around `argparse` in `main`
findings.description: Catching `SystemExit` to turn argparse's exit into a return code is justified by the inline comment. It is a process-boundary handler, so it meets the exception-handling rule. `BLE` does not flag it.

findings.title: Resubmit, ceiling and gate logic fails closed
findings.description:
- **Ceiling rounding.** `_round_up` uses `ROUND_CEILING` on `Decimal`, so multiples are not raised (the tests cover 90 → 90).
- **Resubmit matching.** The key is `(schema, start, end)`. It matches `debug requests` rows because the `range_*` columns are dates. A missing original or a malformed `requested_at` is a stop, never a default.
- **Estimate mode.** `check_ceilings=False` (`--estimate`) skips only the ceiling checks, and scope is still judged.
- **Preflight gates.** `check_gate_issue` and `check_dataset_edge` treat every parse or exit failure as a stop. The tests assert that a `gh` failure is never read as closed.
- **Session buckets.** `_unaccounted` raises on an unknown session bucket instead of passing it.
- **Tests.** They use real CLI renderers (`_cell`, `_product_payload`, `coverage_to_dict`) for fixtures, as the parsing rules require.

structured_findings.summary: Duplicated "want has no end date" check
New tests use bare generics, which strict pyright rejects
Script names no longer match their scope
Resubmit, ceiling and gate logic fails closed
